overview:
The target result is the transform identity with retained permutations. It is an identity relating a discrete Fourier transform of arbitrary length $s$ to transforms whose axis lengths are powers of two, with the coordinate permutations $P_s$ and $P_t$ kept explicit in the formula. Because the permutations stay in the formula, they cancel across a convolution rather than being executed as sorts, which is the purpose of the construction.

The wiki reaches the result in five parts. The first, [Exact integer multiplication](exact-integer-multiplication.md) and [Radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-convolution.md), recasts integer multiplication as a polynomial convolution of digit sequences. The second, [Cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md) and [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md), defines the convolution that transforms compute and the transform itself. The third, [Operator norm](operator-norm.md), supplies the bounds on linear maps that the error analysis needs. The fourth, [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md), replaces a transform of arbitrary length by transforms of power-of-two length, using Gaussian weights to move between the two sets of frequencies. The last part, [Transform identity with retained permutations](transform-identity.md), keeps the permutations in the Gaussian identity, shows the outer resampling maps are contractions, and fixes the normalization by a power of two.

parts.title: Multiplication as convolution
parts.intro: This part recasts multiplication of binary integers as a convolution of their digit sequences. [Exact integer multiplication](exact-integer-multiplication.md) states the problem: the $2n$-bit product of two $n$-bit strings. [Radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-convolution.md) writes both integers as polynomials in a power of two, so that the product becomes a convolution of short coefficient sequences that a transform can compute.

parts.title: Cyclic convolution and transforms
parts.intro: Cyclic convolution is the operation that the transform computes efficiently, since the discrete Fourier transform turns it into pointwise multiplication. [Cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md) defines it with indices wrapping modulo the sequence length. [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) defines the transform over a $q$-th root of unity, normalized by $1/q$, which the rest of the wiki uses at arbitrary length $s$ and at power-of-two lengths.

parts.title: Operator norms and contractions
parts.intro: The error analysis must bound how much a linear map can enlarge a vector. [Operator norm](operator-norm.md) defines the norm of a linear map as a supremum over unit vectors, using the largest coordinate modulus as the vector norm. A linear contraction is a map of norm at most one, and the final part needs this notion to show that its resampling maps are contractions.

parts.title: Gaussian resampling
parts.intro: This part presents the construction that the target result refines. [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md) replaces a Fourier transform of arbitrary length by transforms whose axis lengths are powers of two, with Gaussian weights moving between the two sets of frequencies. It relies on the transforms, the digit convolution and the operator norm from the earlier parts.

parts.title: Transform identity with permutations
parts.intro: This part gives the target result. [Transform identity with retained permutations](transform-identity.md) keeps the permutations inside the Gaussian identity so that they cancel across the convolution. The argument inverts the near-identity operator to isolate the transform, checks that the outer maps are contractions, and absorbs the normalization into a power of two.
